exampleCharacter.name: Example: Character
exampleCharacter.description: A dynamic character on a WORLD_FIXED player brain (W A S D or the arrows: North, West, South, East; Space jumps, Shift runs, C crouches), turning to its last heading, on a ground with crates, stairs and a ramp. exampleGameHud.name: Example: A game HUD

batchedMeshSpike.name: BatchedMesh spike (p375)
batchedMeshSpike.description: p375 Phase 0's spike: 2000 members of 20 geometries with one material, drawn as separate mesh entities (?bmsWay=separate), one baked merge group (baked), one BatchedMesh (batched) whose members are entities with a Transform synced each frame, or one engine batched merge group (engine, p375 Phase 1). ?bmsOrder=grouped adds them by geometry, ?bmsSort=none|range drops three's depth sort or sorts by geometry range, ?bmsCull=false drops per-member culling, ?bmsMove=0.1 moves that share of members each frame, ?bmsShadow=true turns the sun's shadow on, ?bmsCamera=inside looks along the field from its middle, ?bmsColors=true colours the batch's members by geometry, ?bmsHidden=7 hides every 7th and ?bmsBodies=kinematic gives each member a kinematic body (separate and engine), ?bmsMove moving them on fixed steps. ?bmsLod=2|3 gives each member a LOD of that many levels (separate and engine, p375 Phase 2) and ?bmsDolly=true dollies the camera in and out. ?bmsDecals=blend|cutout (separate and engine, p375 Phase 3) replaces the field with a FIFO pool of decals conformed to a heightfield (?bmsDecalPool=128, ?bmsDecalRate=30 a second, ?bmsDecalOrder=join|depth, ?bmsDecalSpawn=rewrite|entity). devTools/bench/batchedMeshSpike.ts measures it.

debugData.name: BatchedMesh spike camera
debugData.description: Placed by batchedMeshSpike.ts at the load: over the whole field, or inside it (?bmsCamera=inside).

instanceStress.name: Instance stress test
instanceStress.description: GPU-driven culling's measuring scene (p354 Phase 0): a square forest of instanced LOD trees (three mesh levels and a cull), cut into tiles of one pool each, with the camera circling inside it. The count comes from ?stressInstances= (or the scene's debug tab), ?stressPath=gpu draws it as one instance set (the compute cull on WebGPU, the CPU backend on WebGL2), ?stressShadow=true turns on the sun's VSM shadow, ?stressLight=spot or point adds a spot or point light's shadow, ?stressViewport=true a picture-in-picture from above, ?stressMove=0.01 moves 1% of the set's trees each frame, and the tab and the profiler show what the CPU path costs per frame: the pool sync, the LOD selection, the render submit.

streamingGrid.name: Streaming grid
streamingGrid.description: World streaming's test scene (p353): a 1 km square cut into 16 × 16 cells of 64 m at rings 1 / 2 / 5. Each cell is code content: a procedural terrain block kept from FAR in (its ground, with a coarse LOD level), scattered rocks whose FAR stand-in is one InstancedMesh of an octahedral impostor, and crates (near only). And JSON content the gather cuts into cells: a beacon in every fourth cell, whose LOD levels give a FAR cell their coarsest level as far groups; a six-piece ruin of a small kit (a block, a slab and a post in two materials) in 16 cells (x and z each -7, -3, 1 or 5), merged AUTO in 32 m cells while near and drawn far as its cell's far groups, each piece its own far entry (p377); and a 320 m wall across six cells, one entity kept while any of them is loaded. The camera flies across it and the cells around it load, switch between their near and far content and unload, fading in and out; the scene's debug tab switches to hovering on a cell boundary, and the Streaming tab's overlay shows the cells' states.

debugData.name: Streaming grid flight camera
debugData.description: The main camera, so the streaming focus: streamingGrid.ts flies it across the grid (or hovers it on a cell boundary). Watch from the debug camera to see the cells load around it.

streamingPhysics.name: Streaming physics
streamingPhysics.description: World streaming with physics (p353 Phases 4-5): 12 × 12 cells of 64 m, each a ground slab, a pile of 14 crates in the tier policy and, along the middle row, a jointed chain lying across the cell's edge, all code content. A kinematic plough, the streaming and the policy focus, mows along the middle row on fixed steps and pushes crates over the cells' edges. Crates are tinted by tier: orange FULL (the policy, near the plough), blue STATIC (the policy, further off in a RESIDENT cell), grey DISABLED (a NEARBY cell's: the scene's nearbyPhysicsTier). A crate belongs to the cell it's in, so one pushed along with the plough stays with it; a chain in a NEARBY cell is STATIC (a jointed body is never DISABLED), and one lying across into a NEARBY cell simulates with its RESIDENT half. Every cell's content is kept from FAR in (rings 1 / 2 / 4): in a FAR cell the crates are purple, REMOVED from the physics world with their state kept, and the chains STATIC, so a crate pushed in a cell that goes FAR is where it was left when the plough comes back.

testDebugScene.name: Optimized assets orientation check
testDebugScene.description: Hand-optimized assets next to their sources, which must look the same: PNG and KTX2 textures (the KTX2 files are encoded flipped), and a GLB with its meshopt and KTX2 copies. Below them, the geometry merge checks: three parts as meshes and merged in code, a MERGED geometry JSON of three imported pieces on two meshes, and a GLB whose 20 pieces the asset pipeline merged into one node, its doors kept apart. Left and right of them, 200 boxes of one material drawn by one merge group. Under the right block, 500 boxes in three materials, merged by AUTO into 12 groups (four 2 m cells). Beside the top row, the material input checks: a texture and its red channel from object-form texture refs (left; the scene doesn't list the texture: the gather adds the material's), and a gradient from an input resolver's bundle (right).
